run_metadata.prompt_or_contract_digest: constitution 0.1.0 / IR 0.1 / role-contracts v0.1 as supplied in envelope

findings.statement: A legitimate objective exists in narrow form: uninterrupted longitudinal observation of an infection's course is described as scientifically unique and not recreatable once treatment alters that course. This is a Level III flourishing good (knowledge) and is not dismissed here.

The requested authority is not observation alone. As specified, it is continued observation coupled with not routinely offering an established, widely available curative treatment to identified infected participants. The knowledge benefit is therefore produced by the withholding, not incidentally alongside it.

Participants did not consent to an untreated-disease experiment and were led to believe they were receiving health care. No assumption-of-risk or waiver argument is available to support the proposal, because the packet records the opposite.

Moral-floor concern, disclosed as required rather than argued around: the proposal uses identifiable persons as instruments for a third-party objective without their consent, and continues their exposure to severe illness and death. Level I prohibitions on treating human beings as disposable resources and on deliberate serious harm to innocents are engaged, and aggregate scientific benefit cannot purchase an exception (IR-02).

The benefit case also fails on its own internal terms. The incremental scientific value of further untreated observation is recorded as uncertain, while the harms avoided by treatment are severe, partly irreversible (death) and extend to non-participants via transmission. The strongest available advocacy cannot establish causal effectiveness proportionate to those costs.

Alternatives are not plainly insufficient for the legitimate objective. Existing accumulated data (A5) is unaffected by stopping; consensual post-treatment follow-up (A4) preserves a genuine longitudinal cohort; independently reviewed, genuinely consented non-therapeutic components (A7) could retain further scientific value. What is lost is specifically the untreated counterfactual arm.

The consequence of inaction points against the proposal rather than for it. Here 'inaction' on treatment is the harm-producing course: harm accrues continuously while observation continues, so delay is itself dangerous (IR-09) and argues for immediate disclosure and treatment offer.

No safeguards are proposed in the packet. There is no described consent process, no independent ethics oversight, no participant appeal route, no exit mechanism and no compensation scheme attached to the requested authority.
Third parties (intimate partners and families) bear transmission risk without any consent or participation, and are outside even the flawed consent relationship with participants.

An internal adviser has raised ethical objections and asked leadership to reconsider; the packet reports no independent review resolving them. Continuation would have the proposing institution act as sole judge of its own conduct.

Advocate conclusion: a constitutionally permissible case for the requested authority as framed cannot be constructed. A strong permissible case does exist for the adjacent objective — preserving and extending scientific value through A2/A4/A5/A6/A7 — and the Advocate affirmatively supports that, so that the outcome is not simple obstruction of the research interest.

principle_assessments.reason: Participants are used as raw material for a knowledge objective they did not accept; worth is being made contingent on research usefulness.
Severe illness, death and onward transmission are foreseeable and avoidable by offering an available curative treatment; the default to preserve rather than destroy is inverted.
Meaningful choice was bypassed: participants believed they were receiving care and were never given the option to accept or refuse an untreated-study role or the available treatment.
Continuation depends on sustaining a false belief about the nature of the programme and on withholding material information about an available effective treatment.

Relevant equals are not treated equally: the untreated cohort is drawn from a historically marginalised population while the accepted treatment of choice is generally available. The rule would not be accepted by those framing it if they occupied the participants' position.
The parties with the least power carry the entire burden; their low power position is what makes continuation practicable rather than what triggers additional protection.
Benefits (scientific dataset, institutional continuity) accrue to the powerful party and to future publics; costs are exported entirely to participants and their families.
Repair is owed for harm already incurred — disclosure, treatment, medical care and compensation — and continuation forecloses it. Feasible remediation is recorded as uncertain.
No material ecological or resource-depletion dimension appears in the packet; effects on future publics are addressed under MC-04, MC-07 and MC-11.

The power exercised over participants is neither necessary nor least-intrusive: A4, A5 and A7 pursue the scientific objective without continued non-consensual exposure, and the harm is substantially irreversible.
The proposing institution would decide on its own conduct; internal dissent is unresolved and no independent review, appeal route or remedy for participants is described.
Overriding an internal adviser's objection without independent examination weakens the mechanism capable of correcting the programme; the raising of the objection is not itself wrongdoing.

information_requests: Whether any participant has been informed of the available curative treatment and of the study's actual nature, and what each participant says they want once informed.
Whether declared conflicts of interest were genuinely sought; the empty conflicts list is unexplained given the institution's stake in programme continuity.
What specific scientific questions remain unanswered, and whether any can only be answered by untreated observation rather than by existing data or treated-cohort follow-up.
Whether an independent ethics body exists with authority over this programme, and what the internal adviser's objection specifically asserts.
Feasible remediation options: treatment provision, ongoing medical care, tracing and treatment of exposed partners, and compensation.
alternatives_or_safeguards: A2/A4 combined and immediate: disclose the relevant facts to every participant, offer the established treatment without conditions, and invite genuinely voluntary continued follow-up — this preserves a real longitudinal cohort while ending the withholding.
A5: continue analysing and publishing from data already collected; no further untreated exposure is required to realise that value.
A3/A6: place any proposed residual research component before an independent ethics body with authority to refuse, with the untreated component suspended meanwhile rather than continued during review.
A7: seek genuinely informed, revocable consent for any non-therapeutic element independently judged permissible, with no linkage between consent and access to care.
Extend disclosure and treatment access to intimate partners at transmission risk, who never had any consent relationship with the programme.
Establish a participant-accessible appeal and remedy route, including compensation for harms already incurred (MC-08, MC-11).
evidence_that_could_change_view: Documentation that participants were in fact accurately informed of the study design and of the available treatment, retained unconditional access to it, and freely chose to decline — which would relocate the question from deception to autonomous refusal.

Credible clinical evidence that the treatment is not in fact established, effective or safely administrable for these specific participants, which would remove the 'available cure withheld' predicate in E3.
Evidence that participants are already being routinely offered the treatment and that the requested authority concerns only observational record-keeping of treated persons.
None of the above are indicated by the packet, and no quantity of additional scientific benefit would change the Level I assessment; only correction of the underlying facts would.
